acceptance_criteria.description: The diff is confined to the six owned sidecar paths and resolves with the existing locked workspace dependencies.

One bounded versioned descriptor is emitted only after distinct literal-loopback bridge/control listeners bind; secrets are independent, redacted, cross-use rejected, and the control secret is never part of the bridge/Lua configuration surface.
Strict bounded control authentication rejects wrong secret/version/epoch, unknown fields, oversized/partial lines, non-loopback peers, and malformed command identifiers without leaking credentials.

The typed state machine relays one valid ready event, applies one idempotent grant as exactly one monotonic CHECKPOINT_GRANTED bridge frame, associates one valid SAVE_DATA_UPDATED event, and returns to idle without permitting arbitrary frames.

Pre-grant abort and decision expiry emit no ROM frame; duplicate commands replay results, changed-body key reuse conflicts, stale/wrong-state input is rejected, and post-grant loss/timeout fails closed.
Bounded backpressure and a single writer preserve checkpoint events and sidecar frame order across sequence wrap/reconnect; replay state is not committed before critical control handoff.

Focused sidecar tests cover descriptor/secrets, strict parsing, ready-grant-save relay, abort/expiry, idempotency/conflict, backpressure, sequencing, and clean task/listener termination while all pre-existing tests remain green.
Formatting, focused/workspace tests, clippy with warnings denied, locked metadata, and diff checks pass without lockfile or unowned changes.

closed_decisions: Keep bridge ABI and protocol version 1 and use the existing empty CHECKPOINT_READY, CHECKPOINT_GRANTED, and SAVE_DATA_UPDATED messages; no generic arbitrary-frame control command or new ROM message is allowed.

Bind distinct bridge and control TCP listeners to literal 127.0.0.1 before printing exactly one bounded strict descriptor. Each endpoint has an independent random 32-lowercase-hex secret; cross-use fails, formatting redacts secrets, and only bridge host, port, and secret may reach Lua.

The descriptor is version 1 and structurally separates bridge metadata from control metadata. Control uses strict bounded JSONL, protocol version 1, a 512-byte maximum line including termination, deny-unknown-fields DTOs, and a handshake binding secret, exact session epoch, and control version.

Expose only typed CheckpointGrant and CheckpointAbort commands keyed by UUID command_id plus the ROM-owned checkpoint key (session_epoch, CHECKPOINT_READY sequence). Emit typed CheckpointReady, SaveDataUpdated, CheckpointExpired, and CommandResult events with fixed status/reason enums rather than free-form strings.

Checkpoint state is Idle -> AwaitDecision -> AwaitSaveData. An exact pre-grant abort clears local pending state and sends no ROM frame. A grant writes exactly one empty CHECKPOINT_GRANTED and is applied only after the full frame is written. A valid empty SAVE_DATA_UPDATED for the active epoch relays the associated ready key and returns to Idle. Decision expiry returns to Idle; control loss or post-grant timeout terminates fail closed.

One task exclusively owns bridge writes and sidecar sequence allocation; one ordered writer owns control events/results. Critical events use bounded backpressure and are never coalesced or silently dropped. Do not cancel partial fixed-size bridge I/O and reuse the stream.

Exact duplicate command IDs replay the prior result without another ROM frame; one ID with a different fingerprint conflicts. Wrong state, stale key, expired key, wrong epoch, nonempty checkpoint payload, partial I/O, and queue saturation have deterministic fail-closed outcomes.

Split ROM sequence freshness inspection from replay cursor commit for checkpoint events so the checkpoint becomes stale only after its critical control handoff succeeds. Preserve existing reconnect and non-checkpoint behavior.
Use only existing locked dependencies; do not add a root dependency or change Cargo.lock.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit root Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, coop-cloud, coop-protocol, coop-server, coop-launcher, ROM C/header/test files, Lua, bridge manifests/docs, integration tests, or orchestration artifacts.

Do not expose an arbitrary frame sender, place the control secret in session.lua, bind wildcard/non-loopback addresses, accept unbounded lines, log secrets, reuse one secret across endpoints, drop critical checkpoint events, or acknowledge a grant before its bridge write completes.
Do not change bridge message numbers, ABI layout, protocol version, or checkpoint payload shape in this unit.
Do not add dependencies, allow attributes, unsafe Rust, staging, commits, branches, fetch/pull/push, remote calls, deployment, or publication.
objective: Implement and verify a distinct authenticated loopback control endpoint that relays the existing ROM checkpoint handshake between the Lua bridge and launcher without exposing arbitrary frame authority or losing critical events.

return_when: Every acceptance criterion is resolved and every required verification command has a recorded outcome.
A required behavior cannot be implemented without a bridge ABI/protocol change, dependency/lockfile edit, or unowned ROM/Lua/launcher change.
A concrete security, concurrency, cancellation-safety, or tooling blocker prevents further progress within the owned files and budget.
